sections.h2: What kind of place is Upper Darby for a home seller?
sections.html:
Upper Darby is a dense, close-in Delaware County township that sits just west of Philadelphia, and its housing stock is mostly older and built close together. The township's own website calls it a first-class township of more than 85,000 residents, packed into 7.9 square miles. That makes it the sixth largest municipality in Pennsylvania and the most densely populated one of more than 5,000 people outside Philadelphia. The 2020 census counted 85,681 people.

The township was split off from Darby Township in 1747, and its boundary was fixed in 1786. Mills along Cobbs Creek and Darby Creek drew early industry, and the 1907 extension of the Market-Frankford elevated line to 69th Street pushed the building boom that produced the row houses and twins you see on streets like Richfield Road. Several boroughs broke away between 1885 and 1911, including Clifton Heights, Lansdowne, Aldan, Millbourne and East Lansdowne, which is now an enclave surrounded by the township.

Neighborhood names matter when you price a home here. Wikipedia lists Aronimink, Beverly Hills, Bywood, Drexel Hill, Fernwood, Highland Park, Kellyville, Primos, Secane, Stonehurst, Terminal Square and Westbrook Park among them, and a Drexel Hill single is a different product from a Bywood row home.

sections.h2: How do transit, roads and schools affect a sale in Upper Darby?
sections.html:
Transit is the strongest selling point most Upper Darby owners have. SEPTA's 69th Street Transportation Center in Terminal Square is the western end of the Market-Frankford Line and the eastern end of the Norristown High Speed Line, and it also serves trolley routes 101 and 102 plus a long list of bus routes. Pennsylvania Route 3 follows Market Street and West Chester Pike across the north, U.S. Route 1 runs along Township Line Road, and U.S. Route 13 clips the far southeast corner.

Public schools belong to the Upper Darby School District. Wikipedia describes 12 public schools plus a kindergarten center serving nearly 12,000 students, with Upper Darby High School, three middle schools (Beverly Hills, Clifton Heights and Drexel Hill) and ten elementary schools. Monsignor Bonner and Archbishop Prendergast Catholic High School is also in the township, and buyers with children often ask which building their address feeds.

  • Check the walk to the El or a trolley stop before you write the listing, since buyers filter by it.
  • Name the elementary school zone in your description, and confirm it with the school district first.
  • Mention off-street parking if you have it. On rowhouse blocks it is scarce.

sections.h2: What does Upper Darby require before a house can close?
sections.html:
A seller in Upper Darby needs a Use and Occupancy (U&O) certificate before settlement. The township's Use & Occupancy page says the permit is required for every sale and transfer, and that it must be in hand before settlement. The seller is the party responsible for getting it.

The application has to reach the Licenses & Inspections office at least 14 business days before settlement, and the township suggests four weeks because of demand. An inspector then calls to set a visit. The visit is visual and non-invasive, and the inspector checks the house against the property maintenance code and township ordinances.

  • Final certificate: the house is compliant and can be occupied.
  • Temporary certificate: minor violations exist, and the buyer must correct them within one year of purchase.
  • Temporary access certificate: substantial violations exist. Current occupants may stay, but no new occupant may move in.

Missing or dead smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and fire extinguishers, structural and electrical hazards, and a failure to file the sewer lateral certification all count as substantial. The sewer lateral certification has to come from an approved Upper Darby contractor. If the buyer agrees to take on repairs, a notarized Letter of Intent goes in with the application. If the buyer named on the application changes, a new application, new fees and a new inspection follow. Payment is by L&I online payment, check or money order. Cash is refused. Call 610-734-7613 to check the current fee schedule.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees come out of an Upper Darby sale?
sections.html:
Realty transfer tax is the big one. Pennsylvania charges 1 percent, and the Delaware County Recorder of Deeds adds the local share. Upper Darby is one of the exceptions to the county's usual 1 percent local rate: its local rate is 1.5 percent, effective January 1, 2022, so the combined rate is 2.5 percent. On a $300,000 price that works out to $7,500. State law makes buyer and seller jointly liable, so your sales contract should say who pays what.

sections.h2: How does Upper Darby bill property tax, and what happens to unpaid bills?
sections.html:
Three separate bills arrive, and the township collects only its own. The Upper Darby Tax Office bills real estate tax, a sewer charge and a trash fee. School tax goes to the Upper Darby School District Tax Office (610-789-7200, extension 3210), and county tax goes to the Delaware County Property Tax Office (610-891-4278).

On the 2026 township bill, real estate tax carried a 2 percent discount if paid before April 1 and face value from April 1 through May 31. A 10 percent penalty applied from June 1 through December 31. Sewer and trash were due at face value by May 31 with the same 10 percent penalty after that. Anything unpaid after December 31 goes to an outside collection agency, and the township stops taking payment. Delinquent amounts become a lien on the property, so a title company will find them and require payoff at closing.

A tax certification tells a buyer's side exactly what is owed. Standard requests take five to seven business days and come back by mail or FedEx, so order one early if you are on a tight closing schedule.

sections.h2: Can I appeal my Upper Darby assessment before I sell?
sections.html:
Yes, and the appeal goes to the Delaware County Board of Assessment Appeals, not the township. Forms are posted on the county's Board of Assessment page, with separate versions for residential, commercial and exemption appeals. Send the completed form to the Government Center Building at 201 West Front Street in Media. Fax and electronic filings are refused, and each form must carry an original signature.

The county warns that postal postmarks can be late. To protect a deadline, hand-deliver the form or ask a post office counter for a hand-cancelled postmark, a certificate of mailing, registered or certified mail, or postage bought at the counter. A decision of the Board can be appealed to court within 30 days of the Board's findings, through the Office of Judicial Support.

Ask the county assessment office for the filing deadline that applies to your tax year, and for homestead questions as well.

sections.h2: Should I list, repair or take a cash offer on an Upper Darby house?
sections.html:
The right route depends on the condition of the house and how fast you need to close. A listing can bring the best price on a sound home in Drexel Hill or Secane, but it carries agent fees, showings and a U&O inspection. A cash buyer can often close without waiting on financing, though the sale still needs the U&O certificate and the sewer lateral paperwork.

  • List it if the house is in good repair and you can wait several weeks.
  • Fix the substantial violations first if you want a final certificate, because smoke and CO detectors are cheap to correct.
  • Sell as-is for cash if repairs, tenants or an inherited property make the timeline hard, and let the buyer take on the temporary certificate work.
  • If the home is a rental, remember the township requires a rental license application for non-owner-occupied properties.

Whichever route you pick, ask for the offer in writing, confirm who pays the 2.5 percent transfer tax, and verify the U&O timeline before you sign.

faqs.q: How long does the Upper Darby use and occupancy process take?
faqs.a: Plan on four weeks. The township requires the application at least 14 business days before settlement and recommends four weeks because inspections are in demand. If the buyer on the application changes, a new application and a fresh inspection are required.

faqs.q: Who pays the Upper Darby transfer tax?
faqs.a: Both buyer and seller are legally liable, and the sales contract decides who actually pays. The combined state and local rate is 2.5 percent, made up of 1 percent to the state and 1.5 percent to Upper Darby.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Upper Darby with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes, in many cases. Minor violations lead to a temporary certificate and the buyer has one year to fix them. Substantial violations lead to a temporary access certificate, which lets current occupants stay but bars new occupants until the work is done.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell a rental in Upper Darby?
faqs.a: A rental license application is part of the packet for any non-owner-occupied property. The township's Housing division runs the rental licensing and inspection program, so ask L&I whether your license is current before listing.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed after an Upper Darby closing?
faqs.a: The deed is recorded at the Delaware County Recorder of Deeds in Room 108 of the Government Center in Media. Transfer tax is collected at recording, and the office accepts recordings between 8:30 a.m. and 3:30 p.m. Your title company normally handles the filing.
